title: Third Floor ticker registry
description: The permanent source of truth for what Third Floor covers, read by the notebook on every monthly run for the life of the project. Deliberately separate from any request or expansion queue: a queue is transient, this is not.

benchmark_anchors.description: Every instrument the notebook fetches as a benchmark. A fund's named_benchmark must name one of these, because a benchmark that is not fetched cannot be computed against.

sec_series_id.description: The SEC's identifier for this fund series. The fee table in the fund's own prospectus is filed under it, which is where its costs are read from (3F D-22).

sec_class_id.description: The SEC's identifier for the exchange-traded share class within the series. Fee-table facts are tagged per class. Seven classes are on EDGAR with no ticker attached, so the identifier, not the ticker, is what finds them.

manual_fees.description: Fee periods recorded by hand where no tagged fee table exists, each with its source: an instrument that was not an open-end fund for part of the archive's history.

sec_series_id.description: The SEC's identifier for this fund series. The fee table in the fund's own prospectus is filed under it, which is where its costs are read from (3F D-22).

sec_class_id.description: The SEC's identifier for the exchange-traded share class within the series. Fee-table facts are tagged per class. Seven classes are on EDGAR with no ticker attached, so the identifier, not the ticker, is what finds them.

category.description: options_integrated is the subject of this app. managed_futures exists so that DBMF, which is not options-based at all, cannot be silently read as one — a label that no longer means what it says is worse than no label.

defined_outcome_caveat.description: True where the fund is a capped or buffered defined-outcome product whose relationship to its benchmark is deliberately nonlinear and path-dependent. Drives a prominent caveat on the report: the reading reflects where price sits in the fund's current outcome period as much as how the fund behaves against the market.

named_benchmark.description: The anchor ticker this fund's own literature points to, or null where it names none. Never a silent default: null REQUIRES benchmark_note, because a fund that declares no benchmark and a fund whose benchmark is untracked are different facts and must not look identical.

benchmark_source.description: How confident the benchmark match is, recorded per ticker rather than assumed uniform, so the site can show how it was arrived at and not just what it is.

benchmark_note.description: Provenance, written in the register of whoever maintains this file: which index the prospectus names, which the marketing names, why this anchor was chosen over another. It names sources and does not simplify them, and for that reason it is NOT shown to a reader — benchmark_note_plain is. Anything present here requires that one.

benchmark_note_plain.description: The same fact in the reader's voice, and the only one of the two that reaches the page. Required wherever benchmark_note is present, because a fund whose anchor is not an exact match must say so to the person reading its report, and must say it in words they were given. Linted in CI against the same banned-word and typography rules as the copy deck (INV-7).
